theory.overview: A stack is a linear data structure that follows the Last In First Out (LIFO) principle. The last element added to the stack is the first one to be removed. Think of it like a stack of plates - you can only add or remove plates from the top. Stacks support two primary operations: push (add to top) and pop (remove from top). They are fundamental for function call management, expression evaluation, backtracking algorithms, and undo operations.

keyConcepts.name: LIFO Principle
keyConcepts.description: Last In, First Out - the most recently added element is the first one to be removed. This is the fundamental property of stacks.

keyConcepts.name: Push and Pop
keyConcepts.description: Push adds an element to the top of the stack. Pop removes the top element. Both are O(1) operations.

keyConcepts.name: Peek/Top
keyConcepts.description: View the top element without removing it. Useful for checking what will be popped next.

keyConcepts.name: Call Stack
keyConcepts.description: Programming languages use stacks to manage function calls. Each function call pushes a frame; returns pop it.

problems.title: Design a Stack with Increment Operation

algorithmSteps.description: Push 10: Add to top of stack
Push 30: Top pointer moves to index 2
Pop: Remove 30 from top, return value
Peek: View top element (20) without removing
Push 40: Add new element after pop

minigame.title: Reverse the Stack
minigame.description: Use Push and Pop operations to transform [3, 7, 2] into [2, 7, 3]. Remember: Stack is LIFO!
instructions: Use Push to add new elements
Use Pop to remove from top
Match the target stack to win
